item.title: Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson on Career Changes, Jason at WrestleMania, Girl Dads & Jabronis | Ep 159
item.description:
92%ers, welcome to another episode of New Heights brought to you by Peloton!
On today’s guest episode, we are joined by the most electrifying man in sports entertainment, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.
Dwayne and the guys talk all about how he left his comfort zone for his new movie "The Smashing Machine," what his life was like playing with Hall of Famers at The U, why his dad didn't want him to step into the ring, his favorite memories from WWE's Attitude Era, what he thought of Jason's appearance at WrestleMania, if Travis is allowed to call people jabronis, life as a girl dad, and more!

item.title: Gameplay Loops Are Out, Chains Are In
item.description:
⚠️ Warning for flashing images. This is a video essay about how designers use visual and spatial metaphors to explain and plan for patterns in games. It discusses the concept of game loops, and action chains, and how these two concepts can be used together to help game developers create repetition, novelty, and meaning in play.
🏥 support IGC on Patreon to join our Discord, where you can get regular game design feedback, playtesting, and other types of community support: https://www.patreon.com/indiegameclinic
👀 Related Materials: Dan Cook's Essay on Value Chains: https://lostgarden.com/2021/12/12/value-chains/ "Concentric Game Loops" Explained with Music: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4T2Ok650IGs&t=260s
🎮 Games Shown; Cosy Grove, Street Fighter, Spelunky, Fallout 4, CastleVania: SoTN, Blue Prince,
🎨 Additional Credits: Art assets in this video (knight coin and zombie pixelart animations) are from the game, Dungeon Delivered!, by Smithy Games. To learn more and download the game for free, visit: https://smithygames.com/dungeon-delivered/. Some music was from videogames, most of it was from my own library. Some of it was too loud. Sorry about that.

item.title: Finding My #1 Pokemon The Most Painful Way Possible | TheCookieRhino
item.description:
Celebrating the next generation of Pokemon by looking back at the mons of old, months after the trend of doing so has died. I'm back baby!
Using the process of elimination was the most painful way of figuring out my favorite Pokemon and I never want to do it ever again.
Hope Scarlet and Violet are good!
